html:
The Beaver Wars were a long run of wars in the Great Lakes and St. Lawrence country of North America, from 1609 to 1701. The Haudenosaunee (Iroquois) Confederacy fought its neighbours for control of the fur trade with Europeans.

Beaver pelts were what Europeans wanted most, and they paid in metal tools, cloth and guns. The Haudenosaunee traded with the Dutch of New Netherland and later the English, who sold them muskets. Their rivals, above all the Wendat (Huron), traded with New France. As beaver grew scarce in their own country, the Haudenosaunee went to war to take hunting grounds and furs, and to take captives to replace people lost to epidemics.

  • 1649: Haudenosaunee war parties broke the Wendat confederacy. Survivors fled west or were adopted.
  • 1650s: the Petun, the Neutral and the Erie were scattered in turn.
  • Peoples further west, such as the Meskwaki and the ancestors of the Ponca, moved west, and much of the upper Ohio country was emptied.

From the 1680s the French and their Native allies struck back deep into Haudenosaunee land. The Great Peace of Montreal of 1701, made between the French and nearly forty Native nations, ended the wars. The map of peoples around the Great Lakes had been redrawn.
